No, you'd instead have to change the lights when they burn out. For the size and brightness you'd need for a motorist to be able to see the lights effectively, you're likely looking at a 15 watt LED. Solar panels today produce about 150 watts per square meter in optimal conditions, but for reasons I outlined in other posts in this thread, a solar roadway would be far below that mark. This means the number of LEDs needed to effectively replace painted lines would consume more power than the solar roadway would produce, resulting in a net loss.
